content: Pakistan face familiar Sri Lanka in Asian Games semi-final Jos Buttler ransacks small chase as England cruise to 3-0 series sweep Athapaththu and Dilhari muscle Sri Lanka past Malaysia in mismatch GS Evo Motors Limited, the authorised distributor of JMEV electric vehicles in Sri Lanka, has launched the JMEV EWIND, a compact electric SUV featuring advanced technology, performance, comfort and safety features. The company said the new model is designed to meet the growing demand for electric mobility in Sri Lanka, combining an aerodynamic exterior with a spacious and technology-focused interior. The EWIND is powered by a single electric motor driving the front wheels, producing up to 108 kW of power and 210 Nm of torque. It can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 8.9 seconds. Depending on the battery configuration, the SUV offers a driving range of up to 610 km under the NEDC test cycle and is equipped with a 70.38 kWh battery. Safety features include six airbags, ABS, EBD, Electronic Stability Programme, Forward Collision Warning, Blind Spot Detection and Lane Keeping Assist. The vehicle also comes with Level 2 Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, adaptive cruise control, a 360-degree camera, dual-screen digital cockpit and over-the-air software updates. GS Evo Motors Chief Executive Officer Priyantha Perera said the launch reflected the company’s aim of making advanced electric mobility more accessible to Sri Lankan motorists. The EWIND is available for viewing and test drives at the GS Evo Motors showroom. It comes with an eight-year or 150,000-km battery warranty and a five-year or 150,000-km vehicle warranty. As Asia continues to account for a growing share of global economic activity, Sri Lanka faces an important opportunity to strengthen its links with regional trade networks, supply chains and economic corridors. How the country can make better use of these connections to attract investment, expand trade and strengthen its position in regional value chains will be among the key questions at the Sri Lanka Economic & Investment Summit 2026, organised by The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce on 12-13 October 2026. Titled “Linking Sri Lanka to Asia’s Growth Networks: Trade, Corridors, and Value Chains,” the session will examine the opportunities for Sri Lanka to deepen its integration with the wider Asian economy and build stronger connections with regional and global markets. The session keynote will be delivered by P.D Singh – Chief Executive Officer, India and South Asia, Standard Chartered Bank. He will be joined for a panel discussion by Chathuranga Abeysinghe – Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, Akio Isomata – Ambassador of Japan to Sri Lanka, Masaaki Kawabata – Chairman – Toyota Lanka (Private) Limited, and Ravi Jayawardena – Group Chief Executive Officer-Maliban Biscuits (Private) Limited. The discussion will consider what Sri Lanka needs to do to strengthen its position within these networks, including improving trade connectivity, attracting investment and creating a business environment that enables companies to participate more effectively in regional and global value chains. (AFP)Sri Lanka’s famed seafood shack Beach Wadiya has hosted royalty including Britain’s Princess Anne and sporting legends such as cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, but now faces demolition under a government-ordered coastal clean-up. The simple Colombo beach restaurant has welcomed a string of celebrities, featured in Madhur Jaffrey’s culinary travels and received rave reviews in international publications, including London’s Financial Times. “Beach Wadiya comes with a lot of history,” said Suhara Chandrasekera, the founder’s granddaughter, now a director of the restaurant. But more than half a century after it opened, the glamour is giving way to grief at Wadiya — which means “shack” in the island’s Sinhala language. The government’s Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management Department gave Wadiya 10 days to pack up and leave — or face demolition. That deadline expired on September 10, but the restaurant is resisting the order to leave. Seven other beach properties were given extensions of about four days to salvage furniture and fittings. A few shops near Wadiya were demolished last month as part of a broader government plan to remove businesses within 10 metres (33 feet) of the shoreline. “There shouldn’t be any buildings within the 10-metre coastal reservation from the shoreline,” Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi told AFP. “We have identified 82 such premises and we are taking steps to remove them.” Beach Wadiya is the only establishment resisting the order and has taken the matter to court. The family of its late founder, Olwyn Weerasekera, argues that the restaurant existed before the 1981 Coast Conservation Act being used to evict them. “We built in 1974, which predates the law that they were talking about… We have permits dating all the way back to 1974,” 26-year-old Chandrasekera said. “In addition to the appeal to the Coast Conservation Department, we also took the decision to file a writ,” she told AFP, referring to a case filed in the Court of Appeal. The family has won a temporary reprieve, with the court ordering the department not to demolish the restaurant for two weeks pending a hearing. When Wadiya was established, the beach was wider and cleaner, with rows of coconut trees, most of which have since been lost to sea erosion. “Right now we have lost two of our huts… We’ve lost parts of our bathroom due to sea erosion,” Chandrasekera said. She said Wadiya was the only restaurant on the beach before Sri Lanka’s tourism boom in the late 1970s. Princess Anne had dinner at Wadiya in 1995. Nepali royals have also dined there. British tycoon Richard Branson visited the restaurant during a family holiday in Sri Lanka in 1992, although the guestbook he signed was washed away in the December 2004 tsunami, according to the family. Indian singing sensation Asha Bhosle, and cricket stars including India’s Rahul Dravid and former Pakistan skipper Wasim Akram, have also dined there. One of the restaurant’s walls has a reproduction of a Financial Times cartoon of a guitar-playing lobster that accompanied a March 1994 food review headlined: “Cook me tender.” The restaurant is best known for offering diners a platter of fresh seafood from which they can choose how it should be cooked. There is no air conditioning and small tables are set up on the beach. An upper floor was added as the beachfront shrank over the years. Experts blame worsening erosion on large-scale land reclamation farther north near Colombo port. If the courts allow the restaurant to survive the government’s coastal clean-up, Chandrasekera says Wadiya will return to its roots. title: BMW R 1350 GS 2027/2028: Rumors, everything we know about the next GS Boxer - CrazyWheels.it
content: The  BMW R 1300 GS marked a clean break with the past: more compact, more responsive, and almost "nervous" in its approach to riding. It has been an undeniable commercial success, but one that left a segment of purists questioning: have we sacrificed too much comfort on the altar of sportiness?Motorcycles With the horizon set for 2027–2028, rumors about the future R 1350 GS are growing louder. As an editor who has followed the evolution of the Bavarian twin-cylinder for decades, here is my technical analysis of what is brewing in Munich. Following BMW Motorrad’s classic chronology, a generational leap to a higher displacement isn't just a marketing exercise; it's about homologation and performance management. If the 1300 reduced dimensions and sharpened the chassis, the future 1350 won't simply need to "go faster." The rumor circulating in circles close to the Berlin plant is clear: the next evolution might not seek a power record, but a return to its "Grand Touring" vocation.Vehicle Specs, Reviews & Comparisons The current R 1300 GS is a scalpel. But BMW knows well that the typical GS customer is a long-distance traveler who doesn't just look for lap times, but the ability to cover 800 km in a day without fatigue. The Engine: An increase in displacement (toward 1350 cc) is likely, not so much to chase extra horsepower (as the 1300 is already at the limit for road use), but to optimize the torque curve at mid-range and comply with future emission standards without losing fluidity. We do, however, expect a new upgrade to approximately 155/160 hp of maximum power. Top Speed: This is expected to remain unchanged at approximately 230/240 km/h (actual). Chassis: We could see less extreme tuning of the Evo Telelever/Paralever system. The goal? More "plushness"—a return to the feeling of "controlled floating" that made the brand famous. We anticipate greater set-up possibilities, with a softer base than the current model; it is likely we will move from the current +/- 2 steps to perhaps +/- 4 adjustment steps for the suspension.Sedans Aesthetics: We may see a return to its "origins" with more protective bodywork for both rider and passenger, and a more classic front end. Historically, BMW does not shorten the lifecycle of its flagship models. A launch planned for 2027/2028 would allow BMW to mature the 1300 platform, integrate all customer feedback, and present a model that isn't just an "uprated version," but a GS that restores the balance between pure performance and the attitude for infinite travel. We anticipate a presentation at the end of 2027 as a MY2028, with availability in the first half of 2028. "We don’t believe we will see a 'less' powerful or performant GS, but a 'smarter,' faster, yet more comfortable one. Our suspicion is that BMW is working on even more precise Riding Mode management, specifically addressing those 'disappointed by the new direction,' with greater adjustment and calibration possibilities. This will make the bike appealing not only to sporty riders but also to long-distance tourists. The 1300 GS is almost a 'toy for sprinting'; the 1350 GS will have the task of returning to the roots of the GS: a fast, comfortable motorcycle, to be used 365 days a year in all asphalt conditions and while riding two-up. If you are waiting to change bikes, don’t rush: the R 1300 GS is today a mature and exceptional product. But if you are looking for the future 'queen of comfort,' 2027/2028 could be the year of the true turning point."BMW Motorrad M We won't sell or share your personal information to inform the ads you see. title: A game developer bought a GeForce 8400 GS for $10 to find the absolute minimum. - GameGPU
content: A Reddit user shared their experience creating a very low-cost benchmark rig to test the compatibility of a game they were developing. To determine the absolute minimum hardware requirements, the developer purchased a discrete MSI GeForce 8400 GS graphics card for $10, including shipping and taxes. This graphics accelerator will serve as the lower performance benchmark for the train simulator, which is being developed using the Godot 4.4 engine and is designed to mimic the visual style of Microsoft Train Simulator and SimCity 4. The enthusiast's test configuration includes an AMD FX-6100 processor, an MSI N8400GS-D512D3H/LP graphics card with 512 MB of DDR3 memory at 1100 MHz and a GPU frequency of 520 MHz, a Creative Sound Blaster Audigy 1 sound card, 8 GB of DDR3 RAM, and a 64 GB SATA solid-state drive. All components are housed in a Rosewill Line-M case, and the base operating system for initial testing was Windows XP Professional x64. The project heavily utilizes the CPU, so the graphics adapter is the least demanding component in the system architecture. The main goal of the build is to test frame rate stability on legacy graphics solutions supporting basic OpenGL standards. A previous prototype of the project already demonstrated around 540 frames per second on an Intel Core i5-2400 and GeForce GT 640. The developer expects to achieve at least 30 frames per second on a GeForce 8400 GS, while reaching 60 frames per second will be the maximum optimization result for the chosen ultra-budget device class. title: GS Retail stock gains after stronger Q2 2026 results - AD HOC NEWS
content: GS Retail stock is supported by solid Q2 2026 earnings, with operating profit rising year on year as reported on August 8, 2026. The shares recently traded on KRX at a level still below their 52-week high, leaving room for further moves. GS Retail stock (ISIN KR7007070006) is trading supported by improved earnings, after the South Korean retailer reported stronger results for the second quarter of 2026 on August 8, 2026, with operating profit rising compared with a year earlier. According to GS Retail's investor information summarizing its latest filings, the company reported consolidated revenue of roughly KRW 2,027.3 billion in Q2 2026, compared with about KRW 1,957.8 billion in Q2 2025, marking revenue growth of around 3.5 percent year on year based on the period data disclosed in August 2026. The same Q2 2026 report shows that operating profit increased to approximately KRW 76.5 billion from around KRW 62.4 billion in Q2 2025, an improvement of nearly 22.5 percent year on year, underscoring a recovery in profitability as convenience-store traffic improved and the supermarket business expanded. In the latest quarter, GS Retail highlighted that its convenience-store division delivered higher sales and profit as consumer demand normalized compared with 2025, while its supermarket and other retail formats contributed to an improved earnings mix, with segment operating profit growth outpacing revenue growth in Q2 2026 relative to Q2 2025. Historical context shows that in fiscal year 2025, GS Retail generated consolidated revenue of more than KRW 7.8 trillion and operating profit of over KRW 260 billion, so the Q2 2026 trends reinforce the company's effort to lift margins gradually from the levels seen in 2025. As of September 18, 2026, GS Retail stock was last quoted on the Korea Exchange (KRX) at around KRW 25,100 per share, compared with a 52-week high near KRW 28,000 and a 52-week low around KRW 21,000, leaving the current price roughly 10.3 percent below the high and about 19.5 percent above the low. Based on recent data for September 18, 2026, this price level implies a market capitalization for GS Retail of approximately KRW 1.7 trillion, with daily trading volume in the hundreds of thousands of shares, indicating that the stock remains reasonably liquid for retail investors. Using the latest trailing twelve-month earnings through Q2 2026, the current GS Retail stock price on KRX corresponds to a price-earnings multiple in the low-teens, suggesting that the market is pricing in modest profit growth rather than an aggressive expansion story. For investors, the key point is that operating profit growth of about 22.5 percent in Q2 2026 versus Q2 2025 comes alongside only around 3.5 percent revenue growth, indicating that margin improvement rather than top-line acceleration is currently driving the investment case. title: Inter-State Council rules amended to allow UT L-Gs to attend meetings if Presidents rule imposed - The Tribune
content: President Droupadi Murmu has amended the rules governing the Inter-State Council which will enable the lieutenant governors of Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir and Delhi to participate in its meetings when President’s rule is imposed these Union territories. The amendment, notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs on September 9 and published on Friday, modifies the Inter-State Council Order, 1990, which the council was established. According to the May 1990 order, the council consists of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all states, representatives of specified Union territories and six Union ministers of Cabinet rank. Its proviso, introduced in July that year, addressed the attendance of a governor when a proclamation under Article 356 was in force in their respective states, or when the order issued by the governor of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir under section 92 of the Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir was in force. In 2019, Jammu and Kashmir was bifurcated into two Union territories, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh, after Article 370 was abrogated. The rule for states under Article 356 and says that “the governor of that state shall be invited to attend the meetings of the Council.” It also adds three separate provisions for Union territories with assemblies. For Puducherry, it says that when an order under Section 51 of the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, is in force, “the lieutenant governor of the Union territory of Puducherry shall be invited to attend the meetings of the council.” “Where an order issued by the President under Section 73 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (34 of 2019) in relation to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir is in force, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir shall be invited to attend the meetings of the council,” it said. The Lieutenant Governor of Delhi will be invited when an order under Article 239 AB is in force, it said. President’s Rule is imposed when there is a failure of the Constitutional machinery in a state or a Union territory. With this amendment, the rules for Inter-State Council meetings now specifically cover the participation of lieutenant governors of Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir, and Delhi when President’s Rule is imposed, while retaining the existing provision for governors of states under Article 356. His writing career began with his first newspaper article at age 15—the same year he inherited his first project car, a 1964 Dodge Dart. That slant-six-powered Mopar was an exceptionally forgiving teacher on the fundamentals of wrenching. And it sparked a lifelong fascination with the forgotten machines, engineering oddities, and the human stories behind technology. Since then, Henry has spent two decades writing about cars, the people who keep them alive, and travel in general. As a freelancer, a staff writer at MotorBiscuit, and features writer at HotCars, he has covered the automotive industry from inside Detroit, attending press events, interviewing industry figures, reviewing new products, and digging into the local history behind obscure enthusiast vehicles. Consumer Reports also analyzed about 380,000 vehicles for its latest reliability survey and gave BMW a 58/100 predicted-reliability score. That landed it in fifth overall and made it the only European brand in the top 10. Lexus eked out a win with a 60/100 score. The question that keeps BMW owners up at night is, “What happens when this wonderfully complicated machine does finally break down?” And to be blunt, the BMW company is making the answer uglier with every new generation of vehicles it builds. The numbers don’t lie. Consumer Reports currently ranks BMW 25th for maintenance and repair cost, while Lexus lands at 15th. What’s the damage? RepairPal’s current Reliability Rating covers 2010–2019 model-year vehicles and puts the average BMW’s annual unscheduled repair and maintenance cost at $968, versus $551 for Lexus. The difference is substantial. BMW locks increasingly ordinary jobs behind paid information, diagnostic software, registration procedures, and specialized equipment. Want to replace the battery on a recent BMW yourself? You can, but on many modern BMWs the job isn’t finished until you electronically register the new battery with the car using compatible diagnostic software. Many of the automaker's recent cars did away with the dipstick altogether in favor of electronic oil level monitoring, a system that has since suffered software issues. Need access to the software to attempt your own repairs? A portal to BMW’s Technical Information System costs $32 for one day, $270 for a month, or $2,700 for a year. No wonder small independent shops must charge high prices to repair your car. On the other hand, if you buy an old Lexus you’re buying into Toyota’s enormous mass-market ecosystem, with related engines, parts, and procedures familiar to many Toyota and Lexus independent mechanics. Sure, BMW has MINI, but there’s far less overlap with a giant mainstream lineup. That gives the aging Lexus a broader service ecosystem before you even get into the parts bill. Lexus didn't build a single halo car to lure away BMW drivers; it took on the entire M car lineup with its F car family. The 416-hp Lexus IS F arrived for 2008 to take on the V8 M3, the 467-hp Lexus RC F dove into M4 territory, and the 467-hp Lexus GS F gave the M5 a naturally aspirated alternative. RepairPal’s published model-level estimates illustrate the value proposition on the used market: $531 a year for an older IS F versus $1,161 for the M3; $754 for the RC F versus $2,781 for the M4; and $499 for the GS F versus $1,173 for the M5. RepairPal says it lacks enough data to issue formal reliability ratings for most of these low-volume models, so treat those numbers as estimates, not gospel. But the broader brand data points the same direction: Lexus led J.D. Power’s 2026 Vehicle Dependability Study with 151 problems per 100 vehicles. Consider one direct comparison. The short-lived V8-powered M3 is notorious because its rod bearings can fail catastrophically, destroying the engine. On the other hand, the IS F’s 2UR-GSE is a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8. It belongs to Toyota’s UR V8 family, sharing the 94-mm bore architecture of the 4.6-liter 1UR but stretching the stroke to 89.5 mm for a 5.0-liter displacement, with forged hardware and Yamaha-engineered performance cylinder heads. Its closest Toyota-badged 2UR cousin powered the Century luxury sedan, while 4.6-liter UR relatives served in Tundras and Land Cruisers. It has a reputation for running forever. When Lexus created the RC F, engineers essentially kept the IS F cylinder block while replacing most other parts, and increasing output from 416 to 467 horsepower. The GS F received the same 467-hp basic recipe, and even the non-F LC 500 later used the 2UR-GSE. And yes, the Lexus V8 still has a dipstick. Repairability gets even more intriguing at the bottom of the lineup. The 2018–2023 IS 350 uses the same 2GR-FKS 3.5-liter V6 engine designation as the contemporary Tacoma. Of course, it's tuned for speed, not tow rating: the IS 350 raises horsepower from the Tacoma's 278 to 311. In short, this is a nimble, compact luxury sports sedan built around the engine block from Toyota's midsize pickup. No, the Lexus F cars aren’t exactly like BMW’s M series. When evaluating the RC F, Consumer Reports lined one up against the BMW M4. Reviewers found the Lexus heavier and a little less sharp. They did praise its firm, direct steering and relentless speed. But in many comparisons, BMW still owns the final few percent of the sports-sedan magic. Lexus prioritized a slightly different experience. The RC F sends a 467-hp naturally aspirated V8 through an eight-speed automatic and available torque-vectoring differential, while the GS F uses the same horsepower figure and a standard torque-vectoring rear differential. But the lineup isn’t all about straight-line speed. Lexus developed the IS F and GS F on circuits including the Nürburgring. They are all serious rear-drive performance cars. The Lexus F cars aren’t just Toyotas with some extra chrome, either. They’re luxury machines. Consumer Reports described the RC F as giving up a little performance in exchange for enough comfort to become a better daily driver than harder-edged alternatives. Factor in the repair-cost spread already examined, and the Lexus starts to look less like the consolation prize for refusing to buy an M car and more like a deliberately different answer to the same question. iSeeCars analyzed more than 395 million vehicles and estimates the average Lexus has a 14.4% chance of reaching 250,000 miles. That makes it 4.2 times as likely as the average luxury vehicle to reach 250,000 miles. In fact, it ranked second among all brands, regular or luxury, imported or domestic. BMW lags far behind with 0.5%. In addition to lasting ridiculously long, Lexus cars have one more advantage that may make them collectible soon. Hagerty’s 2024 survey found 60% of Gen Z respondents interested in owning a classic car. The "classic" they most often inquired about insuring was the NA Mazda Miata. Of the five additional vehicles the generation is already asking about that older drivers seem to be ignoring, 80% are Japanese. No German machines made the cut. I understand the BMW owner’s affliction: I drive one daily. There’s just something about my car that makes the inevitable next repair feel like tomorrow’s problem. Today's problem is hunting for the next empty on-ramp. But immortality will go to the performance cars that remain usable, repairable, and desirable for so long after their warranties expire that they’re worth fully restoring. The Lexus F cars may have been playing the longer game all along. Sources: Consumer Reports, J.D. Power, BMW Group, Lexus, Toyota, RepairPal, iSeeCars, Hagerty We want to hear from you. title: The Adventure Motorcycle That Could Be The Best Long-Term Ownership Bet - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Not every adventure motorcycle is built with long-term ownership in mind. Some are built to rack up miles—not just in terms of range, but over years of ownership. An off-road-ready ADV that looks good on paper may not be one that a rider wants to own for years to come. A genuinely good ADV needs to do more than handle dirt roads. It needs to be comfortable on the highway, manageable around town, and practical enough to live with for years. As the list of these long-term requirements grows larger, the balance becomes harder to achieve for the bikemaker. Luckily, however, some do-it-all long-term ADVs from reputed brands nail that balance, and here's a prime example. The best adventure motorcycles aren’t necessarily the ones with the biggest engines or the longest equipment lists. Firstly, they should still make sense after the first few months of ownership. Then, these bikes are expected to cover a lot of ground, sometimes literally. The same motorcycle might handle the commute on Monday, spend Saturday covering hundreds of highway miles, and then leave the pavement when the route gets interesting. Yes, off-road ability matters, but it’s only one part of what makes an adventure bike useful. A motorcycle that is brilliant on dirt but exhausting on the highway isn’t particularly useful for someone planning a cross-country trip. The same works in reverse: a bike that feels effortless on pavement but becomes unmanageable and intimidating when the surface gets rough isn’t particularly convincing as an ADV. Weight, suspension, ergonomics, throttle response, and low-speed balance all matter. The ability to carry luggage or a passenger without throwing off that balance is another advantage. That balance is what makes an ADV easy to live with. You shouldn’t have to change the way you ride every time the road surface changes. Elsewhere, a strong engine and high peak power make overtaking easier and reduce the effort involved in carrying luggage. Good wind protection matters when the day’s route stretches into hundreds of miles, while comfortable ergonomics can be the difference between enjoying a long ride and simply tolerating it. Lastly, useful electronics, adjustable suspension, and a comfortable passenger seat matter as well. All of these are the nitty-gritty things owners tend to appreciate after thousands of miles. That brings us to the BMW R 1300 GS Adventure. This follows the same basic philosophy that made the previous GS bikes no-brainer picks for long-term ADV aficionados and globe-trotters. The Bavarian manufacturer kept the fundamentals intact while refining the areas that matter most in a long-distance ADV. Accordingly, you can cover hundreds of highway miles, carry its rider and luggage, and still have enough capability when the asphalt ends. The result is an undeniably large and expensive motorcycle, but one that attempts to cover an unusually broad range of riding. The BMW R 1300 GS Adventure is not a cheap motorcycle at a starting MSRP of $23,795. But its appeal comes from how much BMW has packed into one package: a powerful engine, long-distance touring equipment, electronic rider aids, and enough capability to venture well beyond paved roads. So even though the price is hard to ignore, so is the amount of motorcycle you're getting for it. For someone planning to keep the bike for years, you'll simply forget about the price in two or three years. The GS Adventure’s biggest strength isn’t any single feature. It’s how the engine, chassis, suspension and touring equipment work together. The large 7.9-gallon fuel tank makes long stretches between fuel stops easier, while the 8.3 inches of front suspension travel and 8.7 inches at the rear give the motorcycle plenty of room to deal with rough surfaces. On that note, let's dive deeper. At the heart of the GS Adventure is BMW’s 1,300cc air/liquid-cooled boxer twin engine with BMW ShiftCam technology. This motor churns out 145 horsepower at 7,750 rpm and 110 lb-ft of torque at 6,500 rpm, paired with a six-speed manual transmission. 145 horsepower isn't class-leading, but the torque output surely is. Plus, it comes in at under 7,000 RPM, so you will have no shortage of punch at any given RPM. For added convenience, BMW also offers the option of Automated Shift Assistant (ASA), an optional automated manual system that provides clutchless manual or fully automatic gear shifting using electromechanical actuators. Suspension plays a major role in the GS Adventure’s long-distance ability. BMW’s EVO-Telelever front and Paralever rear suspension remain central to the GS Adventure’s handling, while electronically controlled damping allows the chassis to adapt to different loads and riding conditions. The Dynamic Suspension Adjustment automatically adjusts the damping and spring preload, while Adaptive Vehicle Height Control helps make the large ADV easier to manage at low speeds without compromising stability at higher speeds. When equipped with Adaptive Vehicle Height Control, the system raises the motorcycle by 1.2 inches when setting off and lowers it again before stopping. Automatic Load Compensation also detects whether the bike is being ridden solo, with a passenger, or with additional luggage, and adjusts the spring preload accordingly. Lastly, the upright position gives the rider a commanding view of traffic and plenty of leverage over the bike. Wind protection is also present, which should mean less fatigue after several hours on the freeway. The GS Adventure has plenty of electronics, but the important question is whether those features are useful in a motorcycle this large and versatile. Cruise control is particularly useful on long highway stretches, while heated grips can become valuable when the temperature drops or a long-distance trip crosses several climates. On the go, you'll also appreciate the four standard riding modes — Eco, Rain, Road and Enduro — while the optional Riding Modes Package adds Dynamic Pro and Enduro Pro. These modes give riders greater control over throttle response, traction control and ABS intervention depending on the riding conditions. The R 1300 GS Adventure can also be equipped with BMW’s Riding Assistant package, which uses radar technology to provide features such as Active Cruise Control, Front Collision Warning and Lane Change Warning. The 6.5-inch TFT color display serves as the main interface for vehicle information, settings and connectivity. When paired with BMW’s Connected ecosystem, it can also provide access to navigation and other connected functions. There are better motorcycles for specific jobs. A lighter ADV will usually be easier in technical terrain, while a smaller touring bike may be easier to live with every day. The GS Adventure’s advantage is that it can do both reasonably well. It does not need to be the best at what it does, only good enough at everything. It can cover a long highway day without exhausting its rider, carry luggage without becoming completely unwieldy, and tackle rough terrain when the asphalt ends. That's what makes the GS Adventure interesting as a long-term motorcycle. It may be too big, too expensive, and too complicated for some riders, but for someone looking for a single motorcycle that can handle everything from long highway trips to rough trails, its ability to fill so many roles makes it a motorcycle worth keeping for years. title: Karol G’s “Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour” Is a Love Letter to Latinidad, Heartbreak, and the Woman Behind “La Bichota”: Review - Consequence of Sound
content: Log in to track artists, discover shows, and stay in the loop. The stadium-sized journey featured pyrotechnics, surprise guests, and the first full-cast “Bby Wow.” Odds are you’ve heard by now: the biggest headline to come out of Karol G’s first of two nights at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium may have arrived late in the show, when Judeline, rusowsky, and Tainy suddenly appeared alongside the Colombian superstar. Yep, Thursday marked the first glorious occasion when all four partners in crime came together on stage for a live rendition of “Bby Wow,” that global hit you keep bumping into at the gym or the bar. Because the real story of Karol G’s “Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour” (get tickets here) was considerably bigger and, perhaps surprisingly for a stadium show of this scale, more intimate than its biggest surprise guest appearance. Since breaking into the reggaeton industry in 2017 with her massive hit “Ahora Me Llama” featuring Bad Bunny, Karol G has solidified her status as undisputed queen of perreo. Her ever-empowering anthems often encourage women to leave men behind while embracing their most “Bichota” self. But on Thursday night, the Colombian singer-songwriter showed a more nuanced, vulnerable side that further cemented her as a multifaceted superstar. It’s a development that mirrors her latest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. As we noted in our review of the record, the Colombian has now reached the rare level of superstardom that allows her to do pretty much whatever she wants creatively. On the record, she used that freedom to create an album stitched together by heartbreak with the likes of Drake and Bruno Mars playing sidekicks. At MetLife, she built an entire world around the many sides of herself. At first glance, the premise of “Viajando Por El Mundo” (translating to “Traveling Around the World”) is simple. With that title, one might expect a colorful stage and a rundown of songs celebrating different genres and cultures around the world, focusing, of course, on Karol G’s native Colombia. While, to some extent, the show delivered just that, the Medellín native went one step further, bringing a pyrotechnic-filled two-hour show that highlighted who she is not only as a Latina, but also as a woman and as a person who, as her latest album’s title suggests, feels too damn much. At its essence, “Viajando Por El Mundo” is a love letter to Carolina Giraldo Navarro, the real person behind the superstar. The show opened with some of the biggest hits from her Tropicoqueta album: “Latina Foreva” and “Un Gatito Me Llamó.” Behind her, the enormous stage showcased an orange-themed tropical jungle, with its queen, Karol G, at its center as a troupe of dancers gravitated around her. Then, over the next two hours, the singer took audiences on a tour of Latin America, featuring an all-female mariachi band singing “Ese Hombre Es Malo,” Brazilian garota-inspired costumes to accompany “Tropicoqueta,” Dominican bachata for a reimagined version of “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido,” and, of course, Puerto Rico-style reggaeton throughout. It was a production befitting the massive pop star she’s become since she last appeared at MetLife in 2023. “If Karol has taught us anything tonight, it’s that one can travel throughout the world, but your raíces are always in your heart,” a pre-recorded vignette of Mexican-American actor Edward James Olmos roared, emphasizing a message of unity. “Raise your flags and be proud, because it’s time to celebrate where we come from, the sounds that grew up with us and made us who we are. Enjoy, and long live Latino America.” And that’s exactly how the Colombian singer celebrated Latinidad, through a series of deliberate choices that carried additional weight not only as they landed in Hispanic Heritage Month, but also against the backdrop of the current political climate in the United States. Karol often emphasized how proud she is to be Latina, repeatedly mentioning flags she saw from the audience representing different countries in the region. Earlier in the night, however, opener Elena Rose made the evening’s political context considerably more explicit. The Venezuelan singer shared that her photographer had been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as he traveled for the show. You could hear a pin drop as she shared the story with an audience all too familiar with the consequences of the country’s ongoing immigration crackdown. Then Rose roared: “There’s nothing more beautiful than being Latino!” But beneath the intricate dance numbers, sequin costumes, and pyrotechnics, “Viajando Por El Mundo” revealed something more: an honest celebration of self by a singer able to bring together the different parts of her persona. For several parts of the show, Karol took her audience out of the jungle and into her broken heart. Before the set formally began and the stadium transitioned from an orange summer to a deep blue winter, a video of Karol played, where she explained that suffering is part of humanity, and that if heartbreak goes hand in hand with living, she will proudly continue “coleccionando heridas” (collecting wounds). Amid the heartbreak of her latest album, the blue stage once again lit up as Karol celebrated one of its biggest hits, bringing out producer Tainy on a makeshift DJ table alongside collaborators Judeline and rusowsky to perform the song together live for the first time. In no time, the East Rutherford stadium transformed into an Ibiza nightclub, with fireworks shooting into the sky, Tainy bringing a new beat to the hit, and the audience chanting every word of the sad perreo song. The staging made the collaboration feel appropriately international, too: Tainy’s table displayed the flags of Colombia, Spain, and Puerto Rico as the four artists shared the stage. It was the kind of surprise destined to become the headline from the night. But within the larger arc of “Viajando Por El Mundo,” it also made perfect sense: another collision of cultures, genres, and emotions inside a show built around Karol G embracing all of them at once. As Karol continues to establish herself as one of the biggest Spanish-speaking artists of her generation, “Viajando Por El Mundo” suggests that getting bigger hasn’t necessarily meant becoming less personal. If anything, she has used the scale of a stadium show to make a case for the opposite. The era of experimentation in artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly giving way to implementation as companies use the technology to revamp back-office operations, change how users search the internet, and deliver goods to customers. Now a new market is opening as internet platforms introduce consumer AI agents. These agents are being used to help fill online shopping baskets, make travel arrangements, and manage calendars, among other tasks. The velocity of the AI rollout was a surprise at the annual Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference in San Francisco in early September. "I thought we would hear more about what companies were doing in the experimentation phase," says Eric Sheridan, business unit leader of the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications Group at Goldman Sachs Research. "Most companies came with distinct examples of how they're moving from experiments with AI to implementing AI in both their internal operations and workflows, and externally with their customers." The debate around the risks of AI was another major theme at the conference, where leaders of 42 public and private companies shared their perspectives over four days of fireside chats and investor meetings. We spoke with Sheridan about his takeaways from Communacopia, including how AI for consumers will be monetized and the potential impact of a slowdown in AI model development. I think we are at the beginning of a paradigm shift. We are going from a conversational relationship with these agents to a much more action-oriented relationship. Obviously, there are questions in terms of how much trust you place in these autonomous programs and how much you integrate them into your daily life. If you log on and provide an agent with access to your calendar, passwords, and credit cards, you are reducing friction in the program's functionality. If consumers can get over the trust factor, as well as the security factor, that integration will improve dramatically. You could direct an agent to buy you tickets to a major sporting event, find a hotel in, say, Portugal, and confirm and respond to appointments. And that's when you flip the script on the utility layer of the consumer landscape. By this, I mean executing more complex tasks, which generate a higher level of tokens, which are the basic units of data, such as text, that AI models process and generate. More ambitious tasks will be executed by advanced models at the bleeding edge, with subscription tiers for consumers. The mass market for AI agents will be monetized with advertising and subscriptions, much like the way the web operates today. You can buy a premium subscription if you don't want to see ads, and if you do see ads then you are on a basic tier and you're not paying for a subscription. In our research, we have talked about how AI will move from the infrastructure layer to the platform layer and then to the application layer. We think the advent of consumer-facing, action-oriented agentic commerce marks the emergence of the platform layer. Yes, definitely. The creation, placement, and measurement of ads are primarily human-curated activities, even today. We believe AI and machine learning applications across the advertising stack can deliver more efficient and higher-performing ads at a lower cost. They do, but at the moment you can imagine that a lot of cash is getting reinvested back into the build-out cycle behind AI. So seeing that incremental profitability, to some degree, is tougher. The concern among industry employees regarding risks was a major theme at the conference. In terms of what happens next, it's a little early to have a great read on what this debate means. It was interesting to see that many industry leaders sort of agree with the headline idea, which is, "Let's slow the rollout of AI," or "Let's slow the pace or cadence at which we're going to push the frontier forward." When I've looked at industries that go from unregulated to regulated, typically the devil is in the details. Who or what is going to regulate the industry—a government body or a non-governmental organization? What is going to be their mandate? One of the themes that came through at the conference pretty clearly is that most of the compute coming online to support AI is aimed at the supply-demand imbalance that exists today, not some future build-out three, four, or five years from now. And keep in mind that most of those infrastructure projects have already been contracted. No. Our initial take is that the capex cycle through the end of 2027 is likely to remain elevated and in line with our estimates, which are higher than the Wall Street consensus. My colleagues and I estimate that US hyperscalers will deploy $1.4 trillion in capital in 2027. There are constraints up and down the supply chain, including access to memory chips and issues relating to power and land. So even if there isn't a slowdown, there are external factors that could act like a headwind and change how much capital is actually deployed. We received a lot of comments at the conference about the need for deflation in the unit pricing for tokens to drive mass adoption. Yes. In every technology cycle I've analyzed, you need two things—the price of the offering needs to have healthy levels of deflation, and the level of utility must rise. Then you get a lot more folks moving from experimenting with the technology to embracing it in a much wider way. It's important to remember that with AI, there are internal and external components to the technology. On the latter point, think about product creation. Companies are already beginning to use AI in creative ways to engage with their customers and reduce churn. If a platform offers better tools, it's less likely you'll leave for a competitor and more likely you'll be willing to pay for those services. These are dynamics that are very, very constructive in terms of the impact on the whole marketplace. I think there is an interesting iterative loop around AI services that will be a catalyst to watch in the quarters and years to come. This article is being provided for educational purposes only. title: The Opportunities for Investors amid Higher-for-Longer Interest Rates - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The Federal Reserve signaled this week that interest rates could be higher for longer, which may pose a challenge for the broader equity market if tighter policy leads to less consumption, says Anshul Sehgal, global co-head of Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities. However, companies that specialize in computing and data centers could be an opportunity for investors amid elevated interest rates. On The Markets podcast, Sehgal also discusses his take on the latest Federal Open Market Committee meeting and his outlook for longer-term bond yields. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, September 17th. And we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Anshul Sehgal, who is global co-head of Fixed Income, Currencies and Commodities within our FICC and Equities business. Anshul, thanks so much for joining us. Chris Hussey: Okay, this is the third time this year we've had you on after every Fed meeting. We had you out in January, we had you in the April. It's not every Fed meeting, but this Fed meeting we definitely got some action finally. Walk us through it. What do you make from the market reaction so far? We learnt a few things, few key things from Chairman Warsh's presser. Number one, the entirety of the committee coalesced around having two hikes this year. One of them we got yesterday, and likely another one either in October or December. Initially, the market had expected, given what the committee members had said in their speeches, that there would be more dispersion of opinion. That was not the case. They all coalesced, at least for this year. The second thing we learnt is that they believe they're removing a dose of accommodation. It's not that they are moving to restrictive. They believe that the current Fed's Fed funds rate is accommodative, and they are removing a dose of accommodation. He said this three times. Both of those were new pieces of information for the market. In the market's telling, the reason the market's been so frazzled about Fed policy is it's because the market believes that the Fed was making a decision on whether to hike or not based on just the CPI print we got last week or even, say, the last couple of CPI prints, and that is not how the market basically expects the Fed to set policy. In the Fed's telling, it was catch-up. It was that they have missed their inflation target for five years. The employment side of their target has been met, and therefore they need to get a move on. Now, the difference between these two is, like, you look at what changed this meeting, in my mind, compared to what we've heard from the Fed over the last four years, is last four years has all been about if you're going to be running loose fiscal policy, we need to run tighter monetary policy. That is not what the market believes is happening right now because even though fiscal policy is loose, that fiscal expenditure is not really going to labor. If you look at it, primary deficits, which is what the government spends is tracking the same, give or take half a percent rate that it was tracking in 2015 or 2017. What has changed on this side of the pandemic is interest expense or debt servicing costs for the US government. But that does not accrue to labor. That accrues to capital. That accrues to the top decile of wage earners. And for the Fed to hike into that essentially means that labor spending is getting curtailed. So that is not good for the long-term consumption prospects of the US economy, and therefore, what hangs in balance, at least in the market's telling, is you can get closer to your inflation target perhaps sooner by doing all of this, but that would also thwart consumption. Is that what the Fed... Is that what's in the crucible right now? Is that what ... in that debate, it's unclear what the right policy will be. Inflation itself is, at best, a concurrent indicator, likely a backward-looking indicator. Deciding policy just based on that print, again, in the market's telling, might not, might not be prudent. So that's the reason why the markets were frazzled. Equities were down yesterday. They're up today. There's oil prices going up. Like, all of it is just a lot, it's many different dimensions that the market has to handicap. Chris Hussey: Okay. But if we take the Fed at face value, and they're talking about being accommodative, too accommodative, that means rates are going to be higher for longer. What's the path from here for rates? Anshul Sehgal: That's a great question. So, the long bond, as you know, has traded about 5% for a few weeks now. It's the highest yield the long bonds had in over two decades, and understandably, macro markets are quite worried about the long end being unhinged. It's not just a US story, it's a global story. The US Treasury is doing buybacks to, to rein in the yield of the long bond, all of that. That is what we again learned from Chairman Warsh yesterday. He gave clarity on this issue. He does not believe that he has to police the long bond. It's for the market to do. There is also, in my view a good reason for the US Treasury to enact buybacks. A few things have changed over the last decade. Number one, demographics. As the boomers are retiring, the demand for the long bonds not as high from, from their pension savings. Number two, you've got a lot of AI-related issuance, which is all long-dated. And the combination of those things has led to a crowding effect in the long end. So should the US Treasury reduce its long-end issuance when all of this other stuff is going on? It makes some sense to it. Should it be done to expressly with the intent of reining in the long end? Not so much. In markets' behavioral finance, we use the term bandwagon effects that everyone wants to be on the bandwagon that's winning. And therefore, if everyone is worried about deficits or the long end being unhinged, that sort of reduces the willingness of market participants to basically warehouse the long end. Ostensibly, this is all because of debt-to-GDP basically blowing out. People are really worried about the US debt sustainability in the long run. For me, that's a red herring. It's October, it's the new fiscal year. We hear this the start of every fiscal year, that the US is going to be expanding its debt to GDP ratio by 6% to 7%, which is the amount of deficit spending that goes on. But that's not what's transpired over the last four years, because what happens is that the US, at the beginning of the year mark 6% to 7% of additional spending. By the end of the year, if GDP grows by 6% as well, which is what has happened, nominal GDP has grown by about 6% over the last four years, debt to GDP doesn't move that much. In each of the last four years, debt to GDP has worsened by one to one and a half percent instead. So I don't think the sustainability issue is really that credible in the long run. In the near term, what's driving it, the rhetoric is sustainability. The effect, the way it plays out is the bandwagon effect. Like the US had over 200% debt to GDP after World War II. In the ensuing 20 years, that came down to 60% debt to GDP with no austerity, largely because the economy grew its way out of it. So what's endogenous and what is exogenous? Could it be that GDP is just an endogenous effect? Like when the US government fiscally expands more, endogenously GDP goes up, and therefore debt to GDP is more sustainable. It's possible. One has to be open to that. That's what we've witnessed in the last five years on this side of the pandemic. That doesn't necessarily mean that's how it'll play out in the future. The US has run a 3% primary deficit. Should we be that worried about interest expense being 3%? Volker had much higher interest expense. Chris Hussey: All right. So you're a FICC guy, but you're also, you know every market there is, and I love your view on stocks. So let's go to your view on stocks here. What does all this mean for equities, credit, everything else? Anshul Sehgal: I think long-term borrowing costs being in check is a net positive for the equity complex here. What's changed from, say, a year ago to now is that the equity complex is more levered. Largely as I view it, the way the economy's gone on is that over the last few years, the excess interest expense went to the savers. Those savers then lent that wealth to, whether it's a hyperscaler or a Neocloud or pick your sector, essentially then extended credit to that part of the economy. So as of now, the overall domestic equity market is more levered. Anshul Sehgal: But that said, there is also the potential for a general-purpose technology that's going to revolutionize everything we do. Which makes handicapping exactly how macro markets work that much more difficult. It's a more levered system today. We're still very positive on equity, certainly certain parts of the equity market. I think long compute just makes a lot of sense to me here. But does that mean that the broader equity complex should do very well? It's less clear, especially if tighter monetary policy is going to lead to less consumption down the road. Chris Hussey: Alright Anshul, let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Anshul Sehgal: To me, it's being long compute, being long Neoclouds, being long data centers. We get a lot of calls from clients who want to basically buy the long bond north of 5% risk-free yield. It looks pretty attractive. To me, I'm not seeing the asymmetry there. Personally, I think the asymmetric expression is being long compute. These are more levered expressions, of course, but at the same time, we think that they can go up multiplicatively. Whereas if you're long, long bond, especially if you're not doing it on leverage, the amount you can make on that, even if you're right, isn't nearly as much. We're not expecting long end rates to go down to 3%. We think that nominal growth should be north of 5%, and rates have generally hovered about 50 to 100 points lower than that. So the long bond can go to, like, 4.25%, but we wouldn't expect more of a rally from there. Chris Hussey: Such a good point. All right. So much taking place. What are you watching most carefully for markets in the couple of weeks ahead? Anshul Sehgal: I think handicapping the war, because if you take a step back, what we've learned from global central banks is that between certainly the Fed, between tariffs, fuel costs, energy costs going up, even away from the war, the combination of those things, they're not able to underwrite the inflation that comes out of it. So, handicapping what comes out of the Middle Eastern conflict is the number one thing that'll dictate the course of monetary policy and equity markets and fixed income markets. Chris Hussey: Anshul Sehgal, you're a torrent of knowledge every time we have you on. That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for joining us. title: GS, KEPCO Join Forces to Advance Workplace Safety and AI Transformation at SMEs - 스포츠조선
content:
By
																						

													김지민 On the 18th, GS signed a mutual cooperation memorandum of understanding with Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) at the KEPCO Art Center in Seocho District, Seoul, to advance workplace safety and AI transformation among SMEs. The signing ceremony was attended by Kim Jin-a, an executive director at GS, and Yoo Jung-soo, head of KEPCO's SME and Venture Business Office. The agreement aims to support safe working environments and stronger AI capabilities among KEPCO's partner SMEs while laying the foundation for shared growth between the two companies. Under the agreement, the two companies will identify partner SMEs and promote the adoption of AIR (AI Risk Assessment), jointly plan and operate programs to strengthen SMEs' AX capabilities, and establish a performance management system for collaborative projects. AIR is a safety-management AI agent developed by GS employees working at worksites. When work-related information is entered, it analyzes risk factors and safety measures to assist in preparing risk assessment reports. It is currently deployed at more than 250 worksites, where it is used to improve the efficiency of safety-management operations. KEPCO will support the identification of participating SMEs, the selection of SMEs for AIR pilot operations, and implementation of the initiative. GS, serving as the AX implementation partner, will oversee AIR deployment and the planning and operation of the AX capabilities enhancement program. The AX capabilities enhancement program will use GS's AX platform, MISO. Alongside AIR adoption, the two companies plan to link the initiative with AI training to strengthen partner SMEs' ability to apply the technology at worksites. They also plan to develop new cooperation models linking workplace safety at SMEs with AI transformation. A GS representative said, "We believe we can create meaningful change by combining the trust KEPCO has built with its partner SMEs and its understanding of worksites with GS's accumulated experience in worksite-focused innovation." title: GS pursues 15 trillion-won AI data center, seeks big tech leases to fund - CHOSUNBIZ - biz.chosun.com
content: Big tech leases seen as linchpin for financing GS's record AI data hub push The key to the 15 trillion won "Donghae artificial intelligence (AI) data center" that GS Group is pushing to complete in 2028 is whether it can secure long-term lease contracts with big tech. That is because 12 trillion won, or 80% of the total project cost, will be raised externally through project financing (PF). Because it is the largest private infrastructure project ever in Korea, spanning not only an AI data center but also traditional infrastructure, the company must prove the future business profitability to financial institutions. GS is contacting technology companies such as Amazon, Google, and MS to speed up the search for a "deep-pocketed tenant." According to the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 18th, GS Group's holding company GS Co. recently disclosed that it will inject an additional 200 billion won into its subsidiary GS AI Infra, which is leading the AI data center project, by the fourth quarter of this year. It plans to contribute 80 billion won this month first, followed by 120 billion won within the year. Including previous contributions, the holding company's total contribution will be 224 billion won. The company said the 200 billion won in capital will be used to lay the groundwork by investing in land acquisition, permits, and research services. Before full-scale construction begins, the investment will serve as a primer. After that, it plans to carry out paid-in capital increases according to the development stage. The target for equity financing is about 3 trillion won. To spread financial risk, GS established separate special-purpose companies (SPCs) for each project—"Data Center No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3"—under the newly created overarching entity GS AI Infra Co. GS Group's ultimate project goal is to build a 2.4 GW (gigawatt) AI data center. The 15 trillion won the company first presented is the "first-phase target" expense. In collaboration with GS Donghae Power and GS Engineering & Construction, it plans to complete 1.2 GW in stages in Donghae, Gangwon Province. Accordingly, the project size is expected to nearly double in the future. While "80% from others' capital" is a conventional approach, the market is focusing on the scale of this project. Among domestic conglomerates building AI data centers, the sizes ranged from several hundred billion won up to 5 trillion won, including ▲ KT's mid- to long-term project in five-year phases (5 trillion won) ▲ SK Horizon's expansion of existing centers and new construction (3 trillion won) ▲ Naver, each Sejong (650 billion won) ▲ Samsung SDS Gumi Center (427 billion won). For financial institutions to provide the massive 12 trillion won, the key is collateral in the form of big tech's long-term rent and power usage fees. The core tenant (anchor tenant) has not yet been finalized, and the company is said to be accelerating negotiations while contacting multiple global big tech firms. The company especially sees the AI data center, which intersects with related subsidiaries such as AI and construction, as a core future industry and plans to concentrate its firepower. While the goal is to complete it in 2028, the schedule could change as details are negotiated on design methods, cooling methods, and building structures. An industry official said, "Ahead of the election, the Trump administration has seen 'opposition to AI data center construction' emerge as a key issue as big tech demand has surged," and added, "Because the core competitiveness in the AI market is whether power demand can be met quickly, consistently, and stably, most of the supersized 15 trillion won project expense will likely be used to densely fill core equipment such as GPUs, transformers, and cooling facilities." title: Will Higher Costs and Softer FICC Weigh on Goldman Q3 Momentum? - TradingView
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.’s GS third-quarter 2026 outlook suggests some pressure on Global Banking & Markets performance, as softer fixed-income trading and higher expenses could partly offset continued strength in investment banking (IB). Speaking at the Barclays 24th Annual Global Financial Services Conference on Sept. 16, CEO David Solomon pointed to relatively softer activity in fixed income, currencies and commodities (FICC), while broader client engagement and capital-markets activity remained constructive. However, Solomon noted that equity trading has been very strong in the third quarter. The moderation in FICC follows a strong first half of 2026. Goldman generated $6.24 billion in IB fees during the period, up 52% year over year, supported by robust advisory and underwriting activity. FICC revenues totaled $8.60 billion, rising 9%, while Global Banking & Markets revenues climbed 35% year over year to $28.26 billion. The softer FICC backdrop is worth watching because trading remains a key contributor to Goldman’s Global Banking & Markets revenues and provides earnings diversification, alongside investment-banking fees. Therefore, weaker fixed-income trading in the third quarter could reduce the incremental revenue support from Markets, though continued strength in equities should provide a partial cushion, even as advisory, M&A and underwriting activity remains healthy. At the same time, rising operating costs could limit the extent to which strong deal activity translates into earnings growth. At the conference, Solomon indicated that expenses are running higher amid elevated transaction volumes and accelerated technology investments. Non-compensation expenses are expected to increase by more than $500 million sequentially in the third quarter of 2026. Overall, softer FICC activity and a sequential increase in non-compensation expenses could dent Goldman’s third-quarter earnings momentum by limiting the benefits from strong revenue trends. title: Kenny G’s sax to serenade Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair - LI Press
content: The sweet, smooth soprano saxophone sound of Kenny G has enchanted audiences since he stepped into the spotlight with his breakthrough 1986 album, Duotones. His sixth studio album, Breathless (1992), became the bestselling instrumental album ever. Miracles (1994), his first holiday album, sold over 13 million copies, making it the most successful Christmas album to date. He has become one of the best-selling artists of all time and the best-selling instrumentalist in history. Kenny G, born Kenneth Bruce Gorelick on June 5, 1956, has collaborated with a long list of high-profile artists including Aretha Franklin, The Weeknd, Andrea Bocelli, and Kanye West. In November 2025, he made a special cameo appearance in A Very Jonas Christmas Movie, playing a soprano saxophone solo alongside Nick, Joe and Kevin Jonas on the single he co-wrote, “Coming Home This Christmas.” He teamed up with Charlie Puth on Puth’s song “Cry” and followed that up by accompanying Puth with his soprano saxophone at the Super Bowl LX for a performance of “The Star-Spangled Banner.” In his 2025 memoir Life in the Key of G, co-written with Philip Lerman, the musician shared that he was inspired to play the saxophone by watching The Ed Sullivan Show. “I was 10 years old when I picked up the saxophone and I still love playing it,” he said. In his early career, he played in funk bands and backed up artists including Barry White and Liberace. He’s been married and divorced twice and prefers to keep his current relationship private, though digital network creator Katina Ann has shared posts and photos of them together. “I don’t like my personal life to be part of anything that I discuss publicly and that’s only because no one’s that interested,” he said. “I know a lot of celebrities that everyone wants to know everything about, but when I go to my local grocery store there’s no frenzy at all and I’m not complaining.” Like a scientist in his laboratory, Kenny G is always brewing up another musical gem in his studio, conveniently located on the grounds of his LA estate. “There’s a small saxophone part I’m doing for something I can’t tell you about, but I want to make it perfect and it’s literally five seconds of me playing two different times,” he said of his current project. “It will probably take me two hours to get it exactly the way I want it. Obviously it could take me five minutes to do it, but I know myself. I’m going to carve out about three or four hours in my studio today and I’m not going to leave until I get that part done. So that’s a lot of work, but it’s going to be fun.” Kenny G is still enthusiastic about composing and playing his signature saxophone. “I practice three hours every day, usually from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. so I can be at my top,” he said. “That’s what keeps me excited. Every day I’m trying to get better. Every show I play, I want it to be a better show. I’m completely motivated to play my best show.” It was a pleasure to speak with Kenny G before the start of his tour, which lands at Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair on Sept. 26. What about Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair keeps you going back? It’s fun to go back to places we’ve been before. It’s in the round, so that’s not necessarily something that you do very often. It’s a fun place to watch a concert, because nobody really has the advantage since the stage revolves. At some point, you’re going to be right in the front row of it no matter where you are. How did your collaboration with Puth on his song “Cry” come about? He called me and I listened to the song and liked it. That’s all it took for me to do it. I knew who he was, but that didn’t matter. It was the tune that mattered. If it’s a song I like and I feel I can play well on, then I’ll do it. It was easy to play and it was fun. Did it take you only an hour to compose your solo part on “Cry”? Something like that. I didn’t want to get too far into it without him giving me some feedback. So, I took about an hour and then sent it back to him to see if he liked what I did. Then I took the next few hours to fine-tune it. What stands out to you about accompanying Puth on “The Star-Spangled Banner” at Super Bowl XL last February? It was pretty exciting. Everybody wants to be there and you’ve got a backstage pass. It happened fast. There’s a lot of prep work for the two minutes that it takes to do it and it was really fun. I liked playing my little sax parts to go around his vocals. It was really his gig and he was generous to share it with me. How do you decide which artists you will collaborate with? It depends on the vibe of the artist and the song. It’s never about the money. I didn’t get paid for doing the thing with Charlie. I don’t usually charge for solos. It depends on the music and the artist. Why did you decide to bring in Lerman as a co-writer on your memoir, Life in the Key of G? I liked his demo. It was kind of funny and smart. Then I talked to him on the phone and we seemed to have a lot in common. We were about the same age, the same kind of background. The hard part with Phil was him understanding how I make things funny, because he has his own way of making things funny. We had a learning curve on him getting my vibe and then it just worked. You are in the Guinness Book of World Records: 1997 for playing the longest note held on the saxophone using circular breathing. What is circular breathing? I’ll be doing it in the show at Westbury. It’s holding a note for a long time and you breathe at the same time. You don’t stop playing the note to take a breath. It’s a technique that wind instrument players do. Maybe do a duet with Paul McCartney, but I don’t know him. I would never reach out to him. It would have to come from him that he’s doing something and thinks my sound might work for him. That would be great. Maybe be part of a really amazing film score. My wish list would be that somebody like Ron Howard or Steven Spielberg would call me and say give me a theme song for my movie. Is there anything else you would like to tell fans? Come to the show, because as disappointing as this might sound, it’s not all sax. I’ve got a lot of great musicians you will see. We play our music and some great jazz tunes that people will really get into. We love to play our shows and I guarantee you that every show is played like we’re performing at Carnegie Hall with our career on the line. That’s exactly how we play every night. You will be wowed.
